title: Buran, 1988 — the Soviet shuttle that flew once, with nobody on board
sources: Wikipedia: Buran (spacecraft) — the only orbital launch, at 03:00 UTC on 15 November 1988 from Baikonur, uncrewed, on the Energia rocket; it touched down under its own control 206 minutes after launch, in a 61 km/h crosswind, within 3 metres laterally and 10 metres longitudinally of the target mark; the automatic landing system chose an unlikely manoeuvre (estimated 3% probability) on approach; over 1,000 companies across the Soviet Union worked on it; the programme was cancelled in 1993 after the dissolution of the Soviet Union; on 12 May 2002 the roof of hangar MIK 112 at Baikonur collapsed, destroying Buran and killing at least six construction workers
Wikipedia: Buran programme — a response to the US Space Shuttle; the name means "snowstorm" or "blizzard"; carried on the An-225 Mriya
Also on this day (candidates.md, in the app): 1864 Sherman begins his March to the Sea; 2001 the Xbox launches in North America

Images (public domain): Buran on the An-225 and from the rear at Le Bourget, 1989 (U.S. DoD); a 1984 U.S. intelligence artist's concept; the Buran hangar under construction, KH-9 satellite photo, 1983 (NRO); Soviet stamps, 1988 and 1991; Buran 2.01 at the Gromov Institute, 2011
Illustrative stock footage (Pexels, free licence; not of the event): the edge of space, a rocket trail, snow at night

post.facebook:
On this day in 1988, the Soviet space shuttle Buran — "blizzard" — made its first and only flight.

Built as the Soviet answer to NASA's Space Shuttle, with more than 1,000 companies working on it, Buran was lifted into orbit from Baikonur by the giant Energia rocket — without a single cosmonaut on board. 206 minutes after launch it came home, and its computer landed it in a 61 km/h crosswind, within 3 metres of the centre line. On approach it even chose a manoeuvre engineers had rated at about a 3% chance.

It never flew again. After the Soviet Union collapsed the money ran out, and the programme was cancelled in 1993. On 12 May 2002 the roof of its hangar at Baikonur collapsed, destroying Buran and killing at least six workers.

Also on 15 November: Sherman began his March to the Sea (1864), and the first Xbox went on sale (2001).
